Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:10:1.hebrew: א"ל למאי מדמית ליה - לפסולי המוקדשין, דתיפטרינהו מאותו ואת בנו? אותו ואת בנו נוהג בחולין ובמוקדשין, כדמפרש בשחיטת חולין (ד' עח.):
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:10:1.english: He said to him: To what are you comparing it - [To what are you comparing] disqualified consecrated animals, that you would exempt them from [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring"? [The prohibition of] "it and its offspring" applies to non-sacred [animals] and to consecrated [animals], as is explained in [tractate] Shechitat Chullin (daf 78a).

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:11:1.hebrew: א"ה גבי חלבו נמי - אמאי איצטריך אך למיסר? תיפוק לי דאסור, דלמאי מדמית להו? כיון דאמרת: אע"ג דאיתקוש לצבי ואיל, לא נפקי מתורת קדשים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:11:1.english: If so, with regard to its fat as well - Why was “however” needed to forbid [it]? Let it be derived that it is forbidden, for to what would you compare them? Since you said that even though they were juxtaposed to a gazelle and a deer, they did not leave the status of consecrated animals.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:12:1.hebrew: אך ולא אותו ואת בנו - ומסתברא דהיקשא למיפטר מבכורה ומתנות אתיא, ואך למיסר חלבו ואותו ואת בנו; דהשתא מדמינן להו לקדשים גמורין, דאי אמרינן איפכא, לא מדמינן להו לא לקדשים ולא לחולין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:12:1.english: “However,” but not “it and its offspring” - And it is reasonable that the juxtaposition comes to exempt [them] from [the law of the] firstborn and [priestly] gifts, and “however” [comes] to prohibit its fat and [the prohibition of] “it and its offspring”; for now, we liken them to fully consecrated [animals], for if we were to say the reverse, we would liken them neither to consecrated [animals] nor to non-sacred [animals].

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:13:1.english: Only its blood - It is written with regard to a blemished firstborn:

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:15:1.english: The juxtaposition is effective - In that they were juxtaposed to a gazelle and a hart.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:15:2.hebrew: ואהני קרא - דכתיב: "את חלבו לא תאכל". אהני היקישא מכרת, והוה מיסתבר טעמא שפיר, דכי כתיב כרת בחלב — בבהמה הראויה לקרבן כתיב, דכתיב (ויקרא ז׳:כ״ה) "כי כל אוכל חלב וגו'". ואהני קרא למיקם עליה בלאו, דלא תישרייה לגמרי. להכי אפקיה, כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:15:2.english: And the verse is effective - That it would be written: “You shall not eat its fat.” The juxtaposition [to the gazelle and the hart] would be effective [to exempt it] from karet [excision], and the reasoning would make good sense, for when karet is written regarding fat, it is written regarding an animal fit for a sacrifice, as it is written (Leviticus 7:25): “For whoever eats the fat, etc.” And the verse would be effective to establish a negative prohibition regarding it, so that it would not be permitted entirely. For this reason, [the Merciful One] expressed it, etc.:

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:18:1.hebrew: והא תנא - דברייתא דלעיל מפיק חלבו מאך, ורבא היכי מצי למימר דאך לאותו ואת בנו אתא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:18:1.english: But didn’t the tanna - [The tanna] of the baraita above derives [the prohibition of] its fat from [the word] akh [“however”], so how can Rava say that akh comes for [the prohibition of] “it and its offspring”?

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:19:1.hebrew: אילו לא נאמר כו' - והאי דקתני "תלמוד לומר: אך חלק", ה"ק: אפילו לא כתב קרא, מצינא לאפוקי מהכא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:19:1.english: Had it not been stated, etc. - And that which [the baraita] taught, “The verse states: ‘However’ — it divides,” this is what it is saying: Even had the verse not written [“its blood”], I would be able to exclude [its fat] from here.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:20:1.hebrew: רק בכל אות נפשך תזבח ואכלת (דברים י״ב:ט״ו) - ואוקימנא בפסולי המוקדשין לאחר פדיונן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:20:1.english: Notwithstanding, after all the desire of your soul, you may slaughter and eat (Deuteronomy 12:15) - And we have established [this verse as referring to] disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:2:1.hebrew: רב - דלא מוקי מתניתין כרבנן, סבירא ליה כריש לקיש, דאמר התם: לרבנן קדשי בדק הבית כו'. הילכך, לא מיתוקמא מתני' כולה כרבנן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:2:1.english: Rav - Who does not establish the mishna in accordance with the Rabbis, holds in accordance with Reish Lakish, who said there: According to the Rabbis, [animals] consecrated for Temple maintenance, etc. Therefore, the mishna in its entirety cannot be established in accordance with the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:2:2.hebrew: דקתני בסיפא - דמתניתין: "אם מתו יקברו", דקדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:2:2.english: As it teaches in the latter clause - Of the Mishnah: "If they died, they must be buried," [indicating] that animals consecrated for the altar were included in [the requirement of] standing and valuation.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:3:1.hebrew: א"כ - דטעמא דמתני' משום אכילה דקדשים לכלבים הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:3:1.english: If so - That the reason of the Mishnah is due to the consumption of consecrated animals by dogs.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:3:2.hebrew: ניתני אם נעשו טריפה יקברו - דמשמע: אע"ג דמצי למיעבד בהו העמדה והערכה — יקברו, הואיל ולא חזו אלא לכלבים. ומדנקט "מתו", ש"מ טעמא משום העמדה והערכה, (ודלא) כר' יוחנן, דאמר התם: לרבנן, אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי בדק הבית היו בכלל, ומיתוקמא סיפא דמתני' כרבנן, ורישא נמי מיתוקמא כדידהו, דבבעל מום מעיקרו כולהו מודו, ותני: "זו דברי רבי שמעון ומחלוקתו":
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:3:2.english: Let [the mishna] teach: If they became a tereifa, they must be buried - Which would imply: even though one is able to perform standing and valuation upon them, they must [nevertheless] be buried, since they are fit only for dogs. And from [the fact] that it formulated [it as]: "they died," learn from this that the reason is on account of standing and valuation — and [this explanation is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said there: According to the Rabbis, both [animals] consecrated for the altar and [animals] consecrated for Temple maintenance were included [in the obligation of standing and valuation], and [accordingly] the latter clause of the mishna can be established in accordance with the Rabbis, and the first clause can also be established in accordance with their [view], since with regard to [an animal with] a pre-existing blemish, all agree; and [indeed, Rav] taught: "This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him."

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:5:1.hebrew: צבי - כצבי ואיל, ומוקמינא בסיפרי דבפסולי המוקדשין שנפדו הכתוב מדבר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:5:1.english: Gazelle - [Referring to the verse,] “As the gazelle and the hart,” and we establish in the Sifrei that the verse is speaking of disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:5:2.english: Just as a gazelle and a hart are exempt from the firstborn - For “your herd and your flock” is written [regarding the firstborn].

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:6:1.hebrew: ולא אוציא את המתנות - ולקמן פריך: מאי אולמיה דמתנות מבכורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:6:1.english: And I will not exclude the gifts - And later [the Gemara] asks: What is the strength of the gifts over the firstborn?

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:6:2.english: A gazelle and a hart are exempt from the gifts - For it is written regarding the gifts: “Whether an ox or a sheep.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:8:1.hebrew: ומ"ש - מתנות, דלא נפקי מקרא קמא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:8:1.english: And what is different - [About] the [priestly] gifts, that they are not derived from the first verse?

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:8:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: “I will exclude the firstborn, which does not apply equally to all” - For it does not apply to females as [it does] to males.

Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:9:1.hebrew: צבי ואיל - אין אותו ואת בנו נוהג בצבי ואיל, דכתיב: שור או שה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 15a:9:1.english: A gazelle and a hart - [The prohibition of slaughtering] it and its offspring does not apply to a gazelle and a hart, as it is written: "An ox or a sheep" [Leviticus 22:28].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:13:1.hebrew: רק את דמו לא תאכל - האי קרא גבי בכור כתיב, והרבה תימה דלא מייתי "רק את הדם לא תאכל" דכתיב גבי שאר פסולי המוקדשים. ואין להקשות דדילמא איצטריך לחמשה לאוין האמורין בדם, דמפרשי פ"ק דכריתות (דף ד:) — דהא טובא לאוין כתיבי יותר מה': חד בויקרא, וחד בצו את אהרן, ותרי באחרי מות, וד' בראה — הרי ח' בר מהאי דבכור; ושמא דריש להו למילתא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:13:1.english: “Only you shall not eat its blood” - This verse is written regarding a firstborn [animal], and it is very surprising that [the Gemara] does not cite: “Only you shall not eat the blood,” which is written regarding the other disqualified consecrated animals. And one cannot raise an objection [saying] that perhaps [that verse] was needed for the five negative commandments stated regarding blood, which are explained in the first chapter of Keritot (4b) — for behold, many prohibitions are written, more than five: one in Vayikra, and one in Tzav Et Aharon, and two in Acharei Mot, and four in Re’eh — behold, [there are] eight, aside from this [verse] regarding a firstborn; and perhaps [the Gemara] expounds them for another matter.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:17:1.hebrew: ואהני קרא למיקם עליה בלאו - וא"ת: אדרבה, כיון דמהדריה הקרא — הדר לגמרי, אף מכרת! כדתניא לקמן גבי פסולי המוקדשין: "הגוזז והעובד בהם סופג ארבעים", ולא אמר: איתקוש לצבי ואיל ומפקיע לגמרי מלאו, וכי כתיב "תזבח" — ולא גיזה, איסורא בעלמא; אלא אמר: אהדריה לאיסוריה! וצריך לחלק. ומההיא דהגוזז והעובד בהם נמי קשה על מה שפי': טעמו ולא ממשו אסור ואין לוקין עליו, כגון גיעולי עובדי כוכבים — דהשתא כי אישתרי טעם לפגם כמו נבלה מסרחת, וכי הדר אסר גיעולי עובדי כוכבים במדין איסורא בעלמא איכא, לא מלקות; ואינו נראה, דאית לך למימר: אהדריה לאיסורא, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:17:1.english: And the verse would be effective to establish it under a mere prohibition - And if you say: On the contrary! Since the verse restored it, let it return completely, even regarding karet! As it is taught below with regard to disqualified consecrated animals: "One who shears them or works with them absorbs forty [lashes]," and [the baraita] does not say: They are juxtaposed to a gazelle and a hart, which completely removes [them] from the negative prohibition, so that when it is written "You shall slaughter" — and not shear — [this is] a mere prohibition; rather, it states: [The verse] restored it to its [original] prohibition! And [therefore] one must distinguish [between the cases]. And from that [baraita] of one who shears them or works with them, a difficulty also arises against that which was explained: that [something containing only] its taste and not its substance is prohibited but one does not receive lashes for it, such as [flavor absorbed in] the utensils of idolaters — for now, since taste that impairs [flavor] was permitted like a foul carcass, when [the Torah] went back and prohibited the utensils of idolaters in Midian, there is only a mere prohibition, not lashes; but this does not appear [correct], as you must say: [The Torah] restored it to its [original] prohibition, as I explained.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:2:1.hebrew: שייך לקמן רב סבר לה כריש לקיש - בסוף תמורה (שם) משמע כן, מדקאמר רב גידל אמר רב: מאי טעמא דר' שמעון בן לקיש:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:2:1.english: ([This comment] belongs below) "Rav holds in accordance with Reish Lakish" - At the end of Temurah (ibid.), it implies this, from [the fact] that Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav: "What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish?"

Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:6:1.hebrew: מה צבי ואיל פטורין מן הבכורה ומן המתנות כו' - בשמעתין משמע, דאי לא כתב "אך", הוה דרשינן נמי: מה צבי ואיל אין אותו ואת בנו נוהג בו וחלבו מותר. ולעיל בסוף פ"ק (בכורות דף יב.) דרשינן נמי: מה צבי ואיל אין פודין, אף פסולי המוקדשין אין פודין. ותימה: מנלן כל הנך דרשות? דתלתא "צבי ואיל" כתובין, וכולהו צריכי, כדמפרש לקמן פרק פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לג.)! וי"ל, דהתם נמי מפרש: חד לבכורה ומתנות, והיינו כדמפרש הכא — חד מצבי וחד מאיל. עוד מפרש התם (חד לבכורה): חד לכדרבי יצחק ורבי אושעיא, כמו שמפרש ר"ת: המרביע והמנהיג שור של פסולי המוקדשין — לוקה; גוף אחד הן, ועשאן הכתוב שני גופים. והיינו "מצבי ואיל", דחד שור דפסולי המוקדשין עשאן הכתוב כשני גופים, וכשמנהיגו לבדו — כאילו מנהיג צבי ואיל ביחד, וחייב משום כלאים. ואידך: חד לכדר' עקיבא דמתיר אפי' לעובד כוכבים, או לכדרבי אלעזר הקפר פ' שני דחולין (דף כח.): מה פסולי המוקדשין טעונים שחיטה, אף צבי ואיל כן; ומצבי לחודיה הוה ידעינן איל, דמצבי ילפינן כל חיה. ואידך — לכדרב מרי, דמה צבי ואיל דאין פודין. וחלבו מותר ואותו ואת בנו דבעי למידרש בסמוך אי לאו "אך" — היינו מצבי ואיל דדרשינן מיניה בכורה ומתנות, דמשמע שרוצה ליתן להם דין חיה; ואי כתיב "אך", לחייב על חלבה ואותו ואת בנו, כדמפרש: בין לחולין מדמית ליה, בין לקדשים מדמית להו. ובסמוך דקאמר: "וולדן וחלבן היכי דמי, אי דאיעבר ואיתייליד אחר פדיונן, ולד צבי ואיל הוא" — לאו יתורא איכא, אלא ממילא פשיטא ליה דהוי כוליה צבי ואיל:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:6:1.english: "Just as a gazelle and a hart are exempt from the firstborn and from the gifts, etc." - In our sugya it is implied that had [the verse] not written "however" [akh], we would have also derived: Just as [with] a gazelle and a hart, [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring" does not apply to it and its fat is permitted. And earlier, at the end of the first chapter (Bekhorot 12a), we also derive: Just as with a gazelle and a hart one may not redeem [a firstborn donkey with them], so too with disqualified consecrated animals one may not redeem [a firstborn donkey with them]. And it is astonishing: From where do we [derive] all these expositions? For [only] three [occurrences of] "gazelle and hart" are written, and all of them are needed, as is explained later in the chapter [entitled] Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 33a)! And one can say that there as well it explains [that] one [verse is] for [exempting from] the firstborn and the gifts, and that is just as it is explained here: one [derivation] from "gazelle" and one from "hart." Furthermore, it explains there ([deleting:] one for the firstborn) [that] one [verse is] for that of Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Oshaya, as Rabbeinu Tam explains: One who crossbreeds or drives an ox of disqualified consecrated animals incurs lashes; they are one body, but Scripture treated them as two bodies. And that is [derived] from "gazelle and hart," for one ox of disqualified consecrated animals was treated by Scripture as two bodies, so that when one drives it alone, it is as if he is driving a gazelle and a hart together, and he is liable on account of diverse kinds [kilayim]. And the other [verse is]: one for that of Rabbi Akiva, who permits [eating a blemished firstborn] even to a gentile; or for that of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar in the second chapter of Chullin (28a): Just as disqualified consecrated animals require slaughter, so too a gazelle and a hart [require slaughter] — and from "gazelle" alone we would know [about] a hart, as from "gazelle" we derive all wild animals. And the other [word, "hart," is] for that of Rav Mari: that just as [with] a gazelle and a hart one may not redeem, [so too with disqualified consecrated animals one may not redeem]. And [the thought that] its fat is permitted and [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring" [does not apply], which [the Gemara] seeks to derive nearby were it not for "however" [akh] — that is from [the same occurrence of] "gazelle and hart" from which we derive [exemption from] the firstborn and the gifts, which implies that [Scripture] wants to give them the status of a wild animal; and if "however" [akh] is written, [it is] to obligate regarding its fat and "it and its offspring," as [the Gemara] explains: whether you compare it to non-sacred animals or compare them to consecrated animals. And nearby (15b), where it says: "What are the circumstances [of] their offspring and their milk? If it was conceived and born after their redemption, it is the offspring of a gazelle and a hart" — it is not that there is a superfluity [in the text], but rather it is obvious to it of itself that it is entirely [like] a gazelle and a hart.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:9:1.hebrew: אי מה צבי ואיל אין אותו ואת בנו נוהג בו - לא מצי למיפרך: "מה צבי ואיל טעון כסוי, אף פסולי המוקדשין כן?", דבהדיא דרשינן פ' כיסוי הדם (חולין דף פד.) גבי פסולי המוקדשין: "על הארץ תשפכנו כמים", מה כו':
Tosafot on Bekhorot 15a:9:1.english: "If, just as [with] a gazelle and a hart, [the prohibition of] 'itself and its offspring' does not apply to it" - [Rav Pappa] could not object: "Just as a gazelle and a hart require covering [of the blood], so too disqualified consecrated animals [should require] so?" — for we explicitly expound in the chapter [entitled] Kisuy Hadam (Chullin 84a) with regard to disqualified consecrated animals: "You shall pour it out upon the ground like water" — just as [water does not require covering, so too this does not require covering], etc.
